theme: Skia m151 with WASM and performance gains
highlights_headline: 4.151.0 updates to Skia m151 and ports several hot paths from native interop to managed C#.
highlights_body: It also improves WASM exception-handling support with new Emscripten 5.0.6 static libraries for .NET 11, and fixes a native resource leak in SKImage.FromEncodedData.

bullets.detail: Bundles the m151 engine along with several rounds of merged upstream chrome/m151 bug fixes.

bullets.lead: Managed color and pixel-format ports for lower overhead
bullets.detail: Ports SKColor -> SKColorF conversion and single-value SKPMColor premultiply/unpremultiply to managed C#, and adds ReadOnlySpan<char> overloads for SKColor hex parsing.
Makes HarfBuzzSharp.Buffer.AddUtf8(string) allocation-free, removes per-call char[4] allocations in Tag.Parse and SKFourByteTag.Parse, and reads SKShaper glyph results via zero-copy spans.

bullets.lead: Native resource leak fixed in SKImage.FromEncodedData
bullets.detail: Fixes a leak when decoding from an SKData with an SKRectI subset.
Restores SK_ENABLE_LEGACY_SHADERCONTEXT to correct a CPU raster regression.
Adds Emscripten 5.0.6 static libraries built with the new exnref exception-handling model, plus a preview-.NET WASM test job to catch regressions.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Skia submodule bump to drop the SK_BUILD_FOR_WASM redefinition, HarfBuzzSharp allocation-free buffer encoding, and WASM Emscripten 5.0.6 static libraries

preview_summaries.v4.151.0-preview.1.1: Preview 1 opened the line by updating Skia to milestone m151.
preview_summaries.v4.151.0-preview.2.1: Preview 2 added a round of managed-code performance work across SKColor, SKFourByteTag, HarfBuzzSharp.Tag and SKShaper, plus further m151 upstream fixes.
preview_summaries.v4.151.0-rc.1.1: The release candidate added the SKColorF and SKPMColor managed ports, the WASM Emscripten 5.0.6 static libraries for .NET 11, the SKImage.FromEncodedData leak fix, and the CPU raster regression fix.

harfbuzz_summary: Ships the allocation-free Buffer.AddUtf8, the Tag.Parse allocation fix, and the zero-copy SKShaper glyph reads.
